# Story 23 — Provider Messaging Channels: WhatsApp & SMS Windows, Templates, Consent and Delivery Status (Story: 470)

## Prerequisites

- Story for **BE-21 inbound email channel** completed: the inbound webhook + async job + correlation pattern already exists under `app/Domains/Channels/Email/` (`Http/Controllers/InboundEmailWebhookController.php`, `Jobs/ProcessInboundEmailJob.php`, `Services/Inbound/ProcessInboundEmail.php`). This story reuses that shape for provider webhooks — **do not invent a new pattern**.
- Story for **BE-22 web form channel** completed: `app/Domains/Channels/WebForm/` shows the current per-channel folder layout (Models / Services / Http / Exceptions / Retention handler) that this story must mirror.
- Outbound conversation plumbing exists: `app/Domains/Ticketing/Actions/PostTicketMessage.php`, `app/Domains/Ticketing/Actions/TransitionMessageDelivery.php`, `app/Domains/Ticketing/Services/Conversation/DeliveryStateMachine.php`.
- Coordinate with the owner of `app/Support/Http/Errors/ErrorCode.php` before adding new error codes — that enum is a shared contract consumed by `lang/en/errors.php` and `lang/ar/errors.php`, and both files must gain the matching keys in the same commit.

---

## Story Goal

Make WhatsApp and SMS first-class outbound channels that obey provider rules, so a send either succeeds or fails with an understandable, translated reason.

1. A WhatsApp free-form reply attempted outside the 24-hour customer-service window is **rejected server-side** with a distinct error code, and the response tells the agent that an approved template must be used instead.
2. Approved provider templates are stored with their declared variables and rendered **bilingually** (en/ar), same as notification templates.
3. Consent is recorded per customer contact — **explicit opt-in required for WhatsApp**, **opt-out honoured for SMS** — and both are enforced before any outbound send on that channel.
4. Provider delivery receipts arrive on a webhook and move the ticket message through the existing delivery state machine **asynchronously**.
5. Inbound WhatsApp/SMS messages have no subject; a subject is derived from the opening characters of the body.
6. A provider outage degrades gracefully: the outbound send job retries with backoff, the message stays in a truthful state (`queued` → `failed` only after retries are exhausted), and the agent sees that real state.

**Not in scope:** any real provider SDK/HTTP client (Meta Cloud API, Twilio, Unifonic). Ship a transport interface plus a null/log transport, exactly as `app/Domains/Channels/Email/Services/Transport/InboundMailTransport.php` + `WebhookInboundMailTransport.php` do for email. No frontend work.

## Product rules (from story)

| Area | Current behaviour | New behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp free-form reply | No window check; message is posted like any channel | Rejected outside the 24h window from the last **inbound** customer message on that ticket, with a distinct error code and a hint that the approved-template path is available |
| Templates | Only notification templates exist | Provider-approved message templates stored with declared variables, rendered en/ar |
| Consent | Not recorded | `whatsapp_opted_in_at` required before WhatsApp send; `sms_opted_out_at` blocks SMS send |
| Delivery status | Only agent/system-driven transitions | Provider receipts drive `sent`/`delivered`/`read`/`failed` asynchronously |
| Inbound subject | Email subject only | WhatsApp/SMS inbound derives subject from the first characters of the body |
| Provider outage | Undefined | Job retries with backoff; message stays `queued`; only after retries exhausted → `failed` with reason |

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Window boundary exactly at expiry** — a send at `expiresAt()` to the millisecond is treated as **closed**. Enforced in `WhatsappWindowPolicy::isOpen()`; asserted by a unit test with a frozen clock.
- **No inbound WhatsApp message ever** — window closed, template required. Enforced by `expiresAt()` returning null.
- **Ticket has both email and WhatsApp inbound messages** — only WhatsApp inbound messages open the WhatsApp window; the query must filter on channel **and** `MessageDirection::Inbound`.
- **Contact opted out of SMS then replies "START"** — consent is re-recorded via `RecordMessagingConsent`; the opt-out timestamp is cleared, not deleted-and-recreated.
- **Duplicate webhook delivery** (providers retry aggressively) — unique index on `(channel, provider_message_id)` in the inbound table; the receipt path is naturally idempotent because a repeated identical transition throws `IllegalDeliveryTransitionException` and is swallowed.
- **Out-of-order receipts** — `sent` after `delivered` is illegal per `DeliveryStateMachine.php:11–15`; drop rather than error. `read` on SMS is dropped for the same reason (`DeliveryStateMachine.php:29–31`).
- **Provider outage / timeout** — `SendProviderMessageJob` retries on backoff; message remains `queued` and the agent sees `queued`, not a lie. Only the exhausted-retry `failed()` hook writes `Failed` with a reason.
- **Template variable missing or extra** — missing declared variable throws `ProviderTemplateVariableMissingException` before any provider call; undeclared extras are ignored, not injected.
- **Unicode / RTL bodies in derived subjects** — truncation is multibyte-safe (`mb_substr`) and must not split a grapheme; an Arabic-only body must produce a readable Arabic subject.
- **Media-only inbound message with empty body** — derived subject falls back to a translated placeholder; ticket creation still succeeds.
- **Internal note on a WhatsApp ticket** — never routed to a provider; already guarded at `TransitionMessageDelivery.php:23–25`, and the new guard chain must skip internal messages too.
- **Contact has no phone number for SMS** — reject before enqueueing, with the consent/validation error rather than a provider failure minutes later.
- **Half-applied migration state** — the consent columns are nullable and the guard treats "no WhatsApp opt-in row" as *not opted in*, so a partially migrated deployment blocks sends rather than sending without consent (fail closed).

## Migration / Rollback

- Three new migrations: consent columns on `customer_contacts`, `provider_message_templates`, `provider_inbound_messages`. All are additive; **no existing column is altered or dropped**.
- Rollback order is the reverse of creation; each `down()` drops only what its `up()` created.
- **Half-applied state:** if the consent columns land but the templates table does not, the guard chain still fails closed (no consent recorded → WhatsApp sends rejected) and email/portal traffic is entirely unaffected because the guard is a no-op for those channels.
- The new config keys all have defaults in `config/channels.php`, so a deploy without the new env vars boots with the `null` transport and sends nothing to any provider.
